# Git graph syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-gitgraph/grammar/gitgraph.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Git graph syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `gitGraph` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4). mermaid@12 parsed gitGraph with Langium (`gitGraph.langium`, `common.langium`
and `reference.langium` in `@mermaid-js/parser`); the rules below are its token rules, in its
order, and its grammar.

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text; and a line break appended. Keywords are case-sensitive. A word keyword gives way
to a name that goes on past it (`commits`, `cherry-pick03`), so each has a lookahead for the
rest of a name; `title` never does, so a name cannot start with `title` unless it is quoted.

Each statement ends at a line break (or the end of the text); `;` is not a separator.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A git graph is `gitGraph` (with a direction), then statements, one per line; the first may
follow on the `gitGraph` line. The `YAML`, `DIRECTIVE` and `COMMENT` tokens of the lexer are
skipped before parsing.

```ebnf
gitGraph = { NEWLINE } Header { NEWLINE | statement NEWLINE } [ statement ] EOF ;
```

`gitGraph`, `gitGraph:`, or with a direction and its colon: `gitGraph TB:`.

```ebnf
Header @Header = GIT_GRAPH [ COLON | direction COLON ]
               | GIT_GRAPH_COLON ;
```

```ebnf
direction = LR
          | TB
          | BT ;
```

```ebnf
statement = Commit
          | Branch
          | Merge
          | Checkout
          | CherryPick
          | Title
          | AccTitle
          | AccDescr ;
```

`commit id: "A" msg: "Fix" tag: "v1" type: HIGHLIGHT`: a commit on the current branch. The
last `id:`, message and `type:` count; every `tag:` is drawn.

```ebnf
Commit @Commit = COMMIT { ID STRING | [ MSG ] STRING | TAG STRING | TYPE commitType } ;
```

```ebnf
commitType = NORMAL
           | REVERSE
           | HIGHLIGHT ;
```

```ebnf
name = REFERENCE
     | STRING ;
```

`branch dev order: 2`: a new branch at the current commit, checked out.

```ebnf
Branch @Branch = BRANCH name [ ORDER INT ] ;
```

`merge dev id: "M" tag: "v2" type: REVERSE`: a merge commit of `dev` into the current
branch.

```ebnf
Merge @Merge = MERGE name { ID STRING | TAG STRING | TYPE commitType } ;
```

`checkout dev` or `switch dev`: the branch the next statements work on.

```ebnf
Checkout @Checkout = ( CHECKOUT | SWITCH ) name ;
```

`cherry-pick id: "A" parent: "B" tag: "fix"`: a copy of commit `A` on the current branch,
tagged `cherry-pick:A` unless `tag:` is given.

```ebnf
CherryPick @CherryPick = CHERRY_PICK { ID STRING | TAG STRING | PARENT STRING } ;
```

`title Release flow`: the title drawn above the graph (the last one wins).

```ebnf
Title @Title = TITLE ;
```

`accTitle: …`: the accessible title.

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = ACC_TITLE ;
```

`accDescr: …` or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description.

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = ACC_DESCR ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | CHERRY_PICK | `cherry-pick(?![-.\/\w]*[-\w])` |  | `cherry-pick id:"A"`: copies commit `A` onto the current branch. Takes `id:` (required), `parent:` (required for a merge commit) and `tag:`. |
| INITIAL | GIT_GRAPH_COLON | `gitGraph:` |  | `gitGraph:`: starts a git graph. |
| INITIAL | HIGHLIGHT | `HIGHLIGHT(?![-.\/\w]*[-\w])` |  | `type: HIGHLIGHT`: a commit drawn as a filled square. |
| INITIAL | GIT_GRAPH | `gitGraph(?:(?=%%)\|(?!\S))` |  | `gitGraph`: starts a git graph, optionally with a direction: `gitGraph TB:`. |
| INITIAL | CHECKOUT | `checkout(?![-.\/\w]*[-\w])` |  | `checkout dev`: makes `dev` the current branch. |
| INITIAL | REVERSE | `REVERSE(?![-.\/\w]*[-\w])` |  | `type: REVERSE`: a commit drawn crossed out. |
| INITIAL | PARENT | `parent:` |  | `parent: "B"`: which parent of a merge commit a cherry-pick follows. |
| INITIAL | COMMIT | `commit(?![-.\/\w]*[-\w])` |  | `commit`: adds a commit to the current branch. Takes `id:`, `msg:` (or a quoted message), `tag:` and `type:`, in any order. |
| INITIAL | NORMAL | `NORMAL(?![-.\/\w]*[-\w])` |  | `type: NORMAL`: a plain commit (the default). |
| INITIAL | BRANCH | `branch(?![-.\/\w]*[-\w])` |  | `branch dev`: creates the branch `dev` at the current commit and checks it out. |
| INITIAL | ORDER | `order:` |  | `order: 2`: where a branch is drawn among the others (lower first; 0 without one). |
| INITIAL | SWITCH | `switch(?![-.\/\w]*[-\w])` |  | `switch dev`: the same as `checkout dev`. |
| INITIAL | TYPE | `type:` |  | `type: HIGHLIGHT`: how a commit or merge is drawn: `NORMAL`, `REVERSE` or `HIGHLIGHT`. |
| INITIAL | MERGE | `merge(?![-.\/\w]*[-\w])` |  | `merge dev`: merges branch `dev` into the current branch. Takes `id:`, `tag:` and `type:`. |
| INITIAL | MSG | `msg:` |  | `msg: "text"`: the commit message. |
| INITIAL | TAG | `tag:` |  | `tag: "v1.0"`: a tag drawn next to the commit; repeat it for more. |
| INITIAL | ID | `id:` |  | `id: "A"`: the commit's id, shown as its label; a cherry-pick's source commit. |
| INITIAL | LR | `LR(?![-.\/\w]*[-\w])` |  | `gitGraph LR:`: branches run left to right (the default). |
| INITIAL | TB | `TB(?![-.\/\w]*[-\w])` |  | `gitGraph TB:`: branches run top to bottom. |
| INITIAL | BT | `BT(?![-.\/\w]*[-\w])` |  | `gitGraph BT:`: branches run bottom to top. |
| INITIAL | COLON | `:` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accDescr: …` (the rest of the line) or `accDescr { … }` (over lines, to `}`): the accessible description of the graph. mermaid@12's one rule, as two tried in order; the block's `[\s\S]*?\}` is its `[^}]*\}`, written so that line-based highlighters read the block as one span. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr\s*\{[\s\S]*?\}` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ACC_TITLE | `[\t ]*accTitle[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accTitle: …`: the accessible title of the graph, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | TITLE | `[\t ]*title(?:[\t ][^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[\t ][^\n\r]*\|)` |  | `title …`: the title drawn above the graph, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | INT | `0\|[1-9][0-9]*(?!\.)` |  | A branch order: `0` or a number without leading zeros, not followed by `.`. |
| INITIAL | STRING | `"(?:[^"\\]\|\\.)*"\|'(?:[^'\\]\|\\.)*'` |  | A quoted text: `"…"` or `'…'`; `\` escapes the next character, and the text may span lines. Ids, messages, tags and quoted branch names. |
| INITIAL | NEWLINE | `\r?\n` |  |  |
| INITIAL | — | `[\t ]+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | YAML | `---[\t ]*\r?\n(?:[\S\s]*?\r?\n)?---(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `---` … `---` block inside the body: skipped. |
| INITIAL | DIRECTIVE | `[\t ]*%%\{[\S\s]*?\}%%(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `%%{…}%%` left in the text the lexer reads: skipped. |
| INITIAL | COMMENT | `[\t ]*%%[^\n\r]*` |  | `%%` to the end of the line, after other text: a comment. |
| INITIAL | REFERENCE | `\w(?:[-.\/\w]*[-\w])?` |  | A branch name: letters, digits and `_`, with `-`, `.` and `/` inside, not ending in `.` or `/` (`feature/x.y`, `1.0.1`, `hotfix-2`). Quote any other name. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
